children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Wednesday.
WHEAT - Down 1 to 3 cents per bushel
CBOT wheat futures
extended slide to dip to a four-week low, pressured by a rising dollar and hopes that diplomatic efforts could ease Black Sea export disruption linked to Russia's war with Ukraine.
Attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other's ports and shipping have brought the countries' Black Sea exports to a virtual halt, prompting buyers to look for higher-priced alternatives.
While this week's UN gathering has put the spotlight on diplomacy, continued attacks on ports and vessels have tempered expectations of a short-term recovery in Black Sea shipping.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was 2-1/4 cents lower to $7.15 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 4 cents to $7.77-1/4 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last down 1-1/4 cents at $7.35 a bushel.
CORN - Down 2 to 5 cents per bushel
CBOT corn
eased lower after approaching three-year highs this week, with investors waiting to see if a US-China summit on Thursday yields progress in agricultural trade.
Strength in the dollar index

, which has risen to its highest since late July after last Wednesday's interest rate increase by the US Federal Reserve, was also pressuring US grains by making them dearer for overseas buyers. (FRX/)
The corn and soybean markets are also tracking US harvest progress, with recent rain set to curb field work in parts of the Midwest.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last 5-1/2 cents lower at $5.31-1/4 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Down 4 to 7 cents per bushel
CBOT soybean futures
eased ahead of the closely watched US-China summit on Thursday.

Traders are awaiting the outcome of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, with attention on whether Beijing agrees to fresh purchases and removes a 10% import duty on US soybeans.
China's state stockpiler Sinograin on Tuesday announced its second large-scale auction of imported soybeans in September, selling more than half a million metric tons.

A private Chinese crusher bought 68,000 metric tons of new-crop Australian canola for March shipment, after a similar cargo purchased by another private processor arrived earlier this month, trade sources said, in the first such deals since trade was disrupted in 2020.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last 7 cents lower at $13.18-1/2 per bushel.
